result.topic_en: Calculations on a quadratic form in the partial derivatives of a function s (an eikonal/characteristic or geodesic-distance function) with coefficients a_{i,k}. The page introduces auxiliary variables p_i with Σ a_{i,k} p_i p_k = 1 and derives the corresponding characteristic (ray) differential equations.
result.transcription:
$r = \sum \alpha_{i,k} \frac{\partial s}{\partial x_i}\cdot\frac{\partial s}{\partial x_k}$ \quad $s = f(x_1, x_2, \ldots x_n, c_1, c_2, \ldots c_{n-1}) + c_n$

$[-r p_1 x-] r p_1 = \sum \alpha_{1,k} \frac{\partial s}{\partial x_k}$ \quad also \quad $\frac{\partial s}{\partial x_1} = \sum a_{1,k} p_k$
$r p_2 = \sum \alpha_{2,k} \frac{\partial s}{\partial x_k}$ \quad $\frac{\partial s}{\partial x_2} = \sum a_{2,k} p_k$
$\cdot \quad \cdot$
$r p_n = \sum \alpha_{n,k} \frac{\partial s}{\partial x_k}$ \quad $\frac{\partial s}{\partial x_n} = \sum a_{n,k} p_k$
$\sum a_{i,k} p_i p_k = 1.$

$ds : dx_1 : dx_2 : \ldots : dx_n : 2\sum a_{i,k}\, dp_k :$ \quad $\alpha = \sum a_{i,k} p_i \cdot p_k = 1$
$= 1 : p_1 : p_2 : \ldots : p_n : \sum \frac{\partial a_{i,k}}{\partial x_h} p_i p_k$
$\frac{\partial s}{\partial c_1} = \beta_1$
$\frac{\partial s}{\partial c_2} = \beta_2$
$\cdot \quad \cdot$
$\frac{\partial s}{\partial c_{n-1}} = \beta_{n-1}$
$\frac{\partial s}{\partial c_n} = 1$
[-Aus I[?] ... [?] multipl.[?]-]
[-$r p_i + \sum r p_i \frac{\partial s}{\partial x_i} = \sum a_{i,k}\alpha_{i,h}\cdot\frac{\partial s}{\partial x_h}\cdot p_k = \sum a_{i,k}\alpha_{i,k}\frac{\partial s}{\partial x_k}\cdot p_k$-] \quad $\left(\sum \frac{\partial s}{\partial x_h} p_k \cdot a_{i,k}\alpha_{i,h} = 0 \atop k \gtrless h\right)$
[-folglich[?] $\sum r p_i \frac{\partial s}{\partial x_i} = \sum \frac{\partial s}{\partial x_k} p_k \sum \alpha_{i,k} \frac{\partial s}{\partial x_i}\cdot\frac{\partial s}{\partial x_k} = r$-]
[-also $r = \sum a_{i,k}\alpha_{i,k}\frac{\partial s}{\partial x_k} p_k$-]
[-$1 = \sum \frac{\partial s}{\partial x_k} p_k$-]
Wir multipliciren die Gleichungen I$^x$ resp.[?] mit $\sum \alpha_{1,k}\frac{\partial s}{\partial x_k}, \ldots \sum \alpha_{n,k}\frac{\partial s}{\partial x_k}$
$\sum a_{i,k} \frac{\partial s}{\partial x_k}\cdot\frac{\partial s}{\partial x_i} = \sum a_{i,k}\alpha_{i,h} p_k \cdot \frac{\partial s}{\partial x_h}$
$r = \sum r p_k \cdot \frac{\partial s}{\partial x_k}$
$\sum r p_i \frac{\partial s}{\partial x_i} = \sum \alpha_{i,k} \frac{\partial s}{\partial x_i}\frac{\partial s}{\partial x_k}$
$\sum p_i \frac{\partial s}{\partial x_i} = 1$
$ds = \frac{\partial s}{\partial x_1} dx_1 + \ldots + \frac{\partial s}{\partial x_n} dx_n = \sum a_{i,k} p_k\, dx_i$
$ds = \sum a_{i,k} p_k p_i\, ds = d\sum a_{i,k} p_i p_k \cdot s - \sum \frac{\partial a_{i,k}}{\partial x_h} p_i p_k \cdot s - 2\sum a_{i,k}\, dp_i \cdot p_k \cdot s$
$0 = d\sum a_{i,k} p_i p_k = \sum \frac{\partial a_{i,k}}{\partial x_h} p_i p_k\, dx_h + 2\sum a_{i,k}\, dp_k \cdot p_i$
$0 = \sum \frac{\partial a_{i,k}}{\partial x_h} p_i p_k p_h\, ds + 2\sum a_{i,k} \frac{\partial p_k}{\partial x_h} [-p_i p_h ds-]$

methods.what: Quadratic form in the gradient of s with coefficients alpha_{i,k}
Complete integral of the first-order PDE with arbitrary constants c_1,...,c_n
methods.quote: $s = f(x_1, x_2, \ldots x_n, c_1, c_2, \ldots c_{n-1}) + c_n$

methods.what: Introduction of auxiliary variables p_k via the inverse matrix a_{i,k}
Characteristic (ray) equations given as proportions of differentials
Jacobi's method: derivatives of the complete integral with respect to the constants are set equal to constants
Identity derived by multiplying the equations by the sums Σ α_{i,k} ∂s/∂x_k
Total differential of s expressed through the p_k
methods.quote: $ds = \frac{\partial s}{\partial x_1} dx_1 + \ldots + \frac{\partial s}{\partial x_n} dx_n = \sum a_{i,k} p_k\, dx_i$

methods.what: Differentiating the normalization condition along the ray
methods.quote: $0 = d\sum a_{i,k} p_i p_k = \sum \frac{\partial a_{i,k}}{\partial x_h} p_i p_k\, dx_h + 2\sum a_{i,k}\, dp_k \cdot p_i$
